investors.metaDescription: The ProsParity story, our traction, backers and leadership.
investors.title: Financing every life of an EV.
investors.lead: ProsParity finances, services, resells and refinances electric two- and three-wheelers across their whole life.
story: The battery decides the credit risk. It drives both the chance of default and the loss when one happens, and until now it has had no common grade.
Lending is the foundation. We source through dealers, underwrite, collect and service loans funded by our lending partners and our own NBFC.

Battron is the growth. It takes custody of repossessed EVs from any lender, grades the battery and resells the vehicle with a certified grade. Every loan, service job and resale adds to what we know about what an EV is worth.

about.lead: We're building a full-stack digital financing platform that moves credit from lenders to individuals, fleet operators, dealers and OEMs, driving wider adoption of electric vehicles across Bharat for a sustainable future.

timeline.text: First loans, in Bhopal, with Vivriti Capital.
Our own NBFC is licensed, and lends from March.
Battron launches, and we finance its buyers.
Three-wheelers, e-autos and cargo, and two-wheelers all live.

blocks.title: What we do
paras: ProsParity finances, services, resells and refinances electric two- and three-wheelers across their whole life, in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.

We run two businesses that feed each other. Lending sources, underwrites, collects and services loans. Battron takes custody of repossessed EVs, grades the battery, resells the vehicle and acts as an authorised service centre.

howItWorks.metaDescription: Seven stages from lender capital to collection, on our app and on the ground.
howItWorks.title: Digital alone can't see. Physical alone can't scale.
howItWorks.lead: Seven stages take a loan from lender capital to collection. Some happen on our app, some happen on the ground, and we run all of them ourselves.

blocks.title: Follow one rupee of credit
blocks.intro: From the lender to the road, and back.

items.name: Lending partner to ProsParity
items.text: Partner lenders and NBFCs supply capital through origination, co-lending and term-debt structures. We originate, underwrite and service each loan for its full life.

items.name: Walk-in at the dealership
items.text: Most loans start when a customer visits a partner dealership. The dealer is part of the credit decision.

items.name: Dealer-facing app
items.text: Sourcing runs on our own app, operated by our sales team or dealers. No paper forms.

items.name: Digital underwriting
items.text: Bureau, KYC and verification run while the customer is still at the dealership.

items.name: Field assessment
items.text: A field officer visits home or workplace. This is how we see thin-file borrowers that bureaus can't.

items.name: Loan disbursed
items.text: Documentation is completed digitally, and the repayment mandate is set up before funds are released.

items.name: Collection
items.text: Our own tele-calling and field teams work on a platform we built, from allocation to legal. It's never outsourced.

blocks.title: After the loan
paras: Our job doesn't end at disbursal. A battery fault can take a vehicle off the road and put an EMI at risk, so Battron, an authorised service centre, can diagnose and repair it.

If a loan does go wrong and a lender repossesses the vehicle, Battron takes custody, tests the battery and resells the vehicle with a certified grade. About 3 in 4 Battron buyers take a ProsParity loan, and the next owner's loan starts the loop again.

items.name: What digital does well
items.text: Speed, consistency, clean records and no paper forms.

items.name: What digital misses
items.text: Borrowers with a thin file, and work that leaves no paper trail.

items.name: What the field does well
items.text: Seeing how someone really works and earns.

technology.metaDescription: How we built our own sourcing, credit and collections systems for EV lending.
technology.title: Built in-house, not licensed.
technology.lead: Collecting on an e-rickshaw loan isn't like collecting on a credit card. Off-the-shelf systems aren't made for that, so we built our own, and rule changes don't wait in a vendor's queue.

items.name: Sourcing
items.text: A dealer-facing app takes a lead through to sanction for relationship managers and dealer staff: OTP, KYC, product selection and offer. It's built for patchy connectivity.

items.name: Credit
items.text: Two scoring models. One scores customers on bureau data plus field-collected signals. The other scores dealers and OEMs before onboarding, because dealer quality matters so much to the quality of a loan book.

items.name: Core
items.text: Origination and loan management, connected to bureau, KYC, e-sign, e-NACH and payments. Partner-wise books report each lending structure separately.

items.name: Borrower 360
items.text: Customer, vehicle, loan and interaction history on one screen.

items.name: Allocation engine
items.text: Rules-based assignment to tele-callers, field agents and legal.

items.name: Field agent app
items.text: Geo-tagged visits, offline capture, receipts and route view.

items.name: Digital collections
items.text: UPI collect, payment links, and e-NACH presentation and re-presentation.

items.name: Multi-channel campaigns
items.text: WhatsApp, SMS, IVR and voice-bot sequences with reply handling.

items.name: Promise-to-pay
items.text: Capture promises, send reminders and track what was kept.

items.name: Legal and recovery
items.text: Notices, case tracking, settlement and repossession trails.

items.name: Telematics
items.text: Vehicle location and health signals for financed EVs.

items.name: Audit and controls
items.text: Role-based access, logs and RBI-aligned process trails.

blocks.title: Why Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities
paras: Electric three-wheelers are already everywhere in these cities, carrying passengers and goods. But credit hasn't kept up. Many buyers are first-time borrowers with thin credit files, and most lenders can't assess them from a distance.
That's why we work through dealers and with people on the ground. A dealer network lets us reach a town, and a field team lets us understand the borrower once we're there.

blocks.title: Every mile counts
paras: By bridging transportation gaps, reducing pollution and improving the lives of drivers, EV finance can drive meaningful change.
An electric vehicle has no tailpipe, so the air in busy city streets benefits directly. For the driver, lower running costs can mean more of each day's earnings stay at home.

blocks.title: A longer life for every EV
paras: Sustainability doesn't end with the first owner. Through Battron, a used EV gets a tested battery, a certified grade and a new owner, instead of being sold near scrap. Keeping a good vehicle on the road for longer is better for the driver, the lender and the environment.

faq.q: Do I need a salary slip to apply?

faq.q: How do I pay my EMI?
faq.a: Through e-NACH auto-debit set up at disbursal, UPI, or a payment link.

faq.q: I paid twice by mistake. What now?
faq.a: Excess amounts can be adjusted against future EMIs or refunded electronically within one month of your claim being accepted. See our refund policy for details.

finance.detail: Most loans start at a dealership. We check the customer and the dealer, and a field officer can meet the borrower where they live or work, so a thin credit file isn't a closed door.

service.name: Service
service.text: When a battery fault comes up, Battron, an authorised service centre, diagnoses and repairs it.
service.detail: A battery that isn't serviced takes the vehicle off the road, and a missed EMI usually follows. Fixing the fault keeps the driver earning and the loan healthy.

custody.name: Custody
custody.text: When a lender repossesses an EV, Battron takes custody, charges it and tests the battery.
custody.detail: The vehicle is stored under cover and stays on the lender's books until it is sold. Testing the battery sets an anchor price, so nobody has to guess what the EV is worth.

resale.name: Resale
resale.text: The vehicle is sold to its next owner with a certified battery grade.
resale.detail: A grade gives the buyer a reason to trust the price. Graded vehicles sell faster and for more, and the lender receives the proceeds.

refinance.name: Refinance
refinance.text: About 3 in 4 Battron buyers take a ProsParity loan.
refinance.detail: Every loan, service job and resale adds to what we know about what an EV is worth by model, age and battery health. That knowledge shapes the next loan.

lifecycle.close: The next owner's loan starts the loop again.

problem.title: Without a battery grade, a repossessed EV sells near scrap.
problem.body: The battery drives both the chance of default and the loss when one happens. It has no common grade, so buyers can't trust the price and lenders recover little. Grading it gives buyers a reason to pay more, and lenders recover more on every default.

collections.title: Why collections matter as much as approvals in EV lending
collections.summary: Getting a loan approved is only the start. What decides whether EV credit keeps growing is what happens every month after that.
body: When people talk about financing electric vehicles, they usually talk about approvals: who qualifies, how fast, and at what rate. Those questions matter. But a lender decides whether to keep funding a segment by watching what happens after disbursal.

Collecting an EMI from an e-rickshaw driver isn't like collecting on a credit card. Income arrives daily, often in cash. A missed payment may have nothing to do with willingness to pay. The vehicle might be off the road because of a battery fault.

That's why the repayment mandate is set up before funds are released, and why reminders go out before the due date, not after it. A NACH mandate lets a payment be collected automatically from the borrower's bank account, and UPI and payment links give the borrower other ways to pay.

It's also why people still matter. When a payment is missed, our own tele-calling and field teams can find out why. If the problem is the vehicle, the answer may be a service job, not a collection call.
Good collections aren't about pressure. They're about knowing the borrower and the vehicle well enough to keep both on the road.

batteryRisk.title: Why the battery decides the credit risk
batteryRisk.summary: In an EV, one component drives both the chance of default and the loss when one happens.
body: In a petrol or diesel vehicle, a lender can look up a rough resale value. An electric vehicle is different. Its value depends heavily on the battery, and until now that battery has had no common grade.

The trouble often starts quietly. A battery isn't serviced. The vehicle goes off the road. The driver stops earning and misses an EMI, usually before any credit bureau signal appears. The loan defaults, and the vehicle is repossessed.

Then comes the second problem. With no grade, a buyer can't tell a healthy battery from a worn one, so the vehicle sells near scrap. Lenders see that and either stay away or add a buffer to their pricing. They set that buffer without a battery grade, so no lender knows whether it covers the risk.
Grading changes this. When a buyer can trust the battery, they'll pay more and buy sooner. Lenders recover more on every default, and that makes it easier to lend in the first place.

Every loan, service job and resale also adds to what is known about how an EV holds its value by model, age and battery health. The more vehicles go through the loop, the better the next loan can be priced.

battronLaunch.title: Battron launches to give used EVs a trusted price
battronLaunch.summary: Our resale platform takes custody of repossessed EVs, grades the battery and resells the vehicle with a certified grade.
body: In April 2026 we launched Battron, a resale platform for used EVs, starting with repossessed vehicles from any lender.
Lenders hand over a repossessed EV. Battron charges it, stores it under cover and tests the battery to set an anchor price. The vehicle stays on the lender's books until it is sold.

Battron then sells the vehicle to its next owner with a certified grade. ProsParity can finance the buyer, and the lender receives the proceeds. Battron also acts as an authorised service centre, diagnosing and repairing battery faults for EV owners.
It matters because a repossessed EV has often sold for far less than it should. A grade gives buyers a reason to trust the price, which helps vehicles sell faster and for more.

rbiDirections.title: RBI tightens disclosure norms for digital lending
rbiDirections.summary: The Digital Lending Directions, 2025 bring earlier rules together. For borrowers, the main change is seeing the full cost of a loan before agreeing to it.
body: On 8 May 2025 the Reserve Bank of India issued the Digital Lending Directions, 2025. They replace the 2022 guidelines on digital lending and the 2023 guidelines on default loss guarantees with a single set of rules.

For a borrower, the most useful part is the Key Fact Statement. Before a loan is finalised, you should receive this short document in a standard format. It sets out the terms of the loan, including the annual percentage rate and other charges, so you can compare offers and see the real cost.

Our advice is simple. Read the Key Fact Statement before you agree to anything. If a number isn't clear, ask. And if you ever have a complaint, every regulated lender must give you a way to raise it, with the RBI Ombudsman available after that.
This article is a plain-language summary, not legal advice. Please read the RBI's directions for the exact wording.
